sections.text: ## The Big Picture

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text: A reef is not one ecosystem — it is a mosaic of overlapping communities shaped by water energy, depth, light, and substrate. Understanding reef ecology requires layering three frameworks: spatial zonation (where), trophic structure (who eats whom), and temporal dynamics (day vs. night, season, recruitment pulses).

sections.text: ## Zone-by-Zone Detail

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text: ### Reef Flat

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text: Exposed at low tide on many reefs. Conditions: high temperature, low salinity (rain), desiccation stress. Dominated by encrusting coralline algae, massive Porites, hardy sea cucumbers, urchins, and small fish. Surge channels cut through the flat allow water circulation. Habitat: foraging ground for wrasses, goatfish, surgeonfish during tidal flooding.

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text: ### Reef Crest

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text: The highest-energy zone — breaking wave energy dissipated here. Dominated by encrusting CCA (mechanically strongest), encrusting *Montipora*, *Pocillopora* (branchy but sturdy). Surge channels are cut by the wave energy itself. Very few fish tolerate this zone full-time, though some wrasses and surgeonfish forage at the margins.

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text: ### Fore-Reef Slope (2–20 m)

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
**Maximum coral cover and fish diversity.** Gradient of species by depth:
- 0–5 m: *Pocillopora*, *Stylophora*, table *Acropora*, massive corals
- 5–15 m: Peak diversity; *Acropora* thickets, massive corals, gorgonians beginning
- 15–25 m: Plating *Montipora*, *Turbinaria*, deep-adapted *Porites*

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text: ### Reef Wall / Deep Slope (>20 m)

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text: Plating and foliose corals maximize surface area for light capture. Gorgonians, black corals (antipatharians), sponges increase in importance. Commercially important fish species (grouper, snapper spawning aggregations). At 30–150 m: mesophotic zone — distinct community, cooler, thermally buffered.

```
sections.text: ## Herbivory — The Critical Reef Process

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text: Without herbivory, macroalgae overgrow coral and prevent recruitment. This is the most important regulatory process on reefs after coral growth itself.

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
```
HERBIVORY DYNAMICS
===================

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
ALGAE grow on any hard substrate vacated by coral
     ↓ if herbivory is intact
HERBIVORES remove algae and keep substrate open for coral larvae

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text: KEY HERBIVORES:

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
PARROTFISH (Scaridae):
  - Bite coral substrate with fused beak (scraping + excavating)
  - Produce sand: 1 large parrotfish = ~90 kg sand/yr
  - Excavating species bite into live coral framework (bioerosion)
  - Critical for both algae removal AND creating settlement substrate
  - Loss → algal accumulation; reduced coral recruitment

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
SURGEONFISH (Acanthuridae):
  - Browsers and grazers of algal turfs
  - Less dramatic per-individual impact but enormous biomass
  - High site fidelity; important in back-reef / flat zones

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
URCHINS (primarily Diadema antillarum, Caribbean):
  - Spiny sea urchins graze bare rock continuously
  - Caribbean reefs: critical after parrotfish removal by fishing
  - 1983: Mass mortality of Diadema (disease) across entire Caribbean
  - Result: immediate macroalgal bloom → reef phase shift in many areas
  - D. antillarum now recovering in some areas; still at <20% of 1980s abundance

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
ALGAL PHASE SHIFT:
  Intact herbivory    →  Coral-dominated reef (10–50% coral cover)
  Reduced herbivory   →  Transitional ("rubble reef")
  No effective herbivy→  Algal-dominated reef (macroalgae >80% cover)
  Once shifted, extremely difficult to reverse without active intervention
```

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna
```

```
sections.text: **Acanthaster planci** (crown-of-thorns, CoTS) deserves special mention: it is native to Indo-Pacific reefs and normally present at low density (0.1–6 per km²). At outbreak densities (>15 per km²), each individual consumes up to 6 m² of live coral per year. A single outbreak on a small reef can remove >50% of live coral cover in 2 years.

sections.text: ## Cryptic Fauna

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text: The reef is mostly invisible:

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
```
CRYPTOFAUNA — THE HIDDEN REEF
================================

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
Estimated 50–70% of reef species are cryptic
(living in crevices, rubble, under coral heads)

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
FRAMEWORK CRYPTOFAUNA
  - Sponges (boring into skeleton)
  - Polychaete worms (Christmas tree worms = Spirobranchus in Porites)
  - Crabs (Trapezia spp. in Acropora — obligate mutualists; defend coral)
  - Shrimps (Alpheid pistol shrimp; snapping mantis shrimp)
  - Brittle stars (Ophiuroidea) in crevices — emerge at night
  - Small blennies, gobies (hundreds of cryptic species)
  - Nudibranchs

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
RUBBLE ZONE
  - Juvenile fish (rubble = nursery habitat)
  - Heart urchins (infaunal)
  - Bivalves (Tridacna giant clams = framework)

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
CRYPTOFAUNA FUNCTIONS:
  - Bioerosion (sponges, urchins) = ~30% of CaCO₃ budget
  - Food web nodes (massive invertebrate biomass invisible to surveys)
  - Cleaning stations (cleaner shrimps, cleaner wrasse)
  - Coral defense (Trapezia crabs defend their Acropora host)
```

sections.text: ## Day vs. Night Communities

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna
Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
DAY COMMUNITY:
  - Visual predators (barracuda, jacks) active
  - Planktivores (Chromis, Anthias) hover above coral feeding on zooplankton
  - Herbivores (parrotfish, surgeonfish) actively graze
  - Butterflyfishes forage on coral polyps
  - Colors vivid (many fish have UV vision)

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
NIGHT COMMUNITY:
  - Nocturnal predators emerge (lobster, octopus, cone snails)
  - Coral polyps EXTEND TENTACLES — active predation on zooplankton
  - Parrotfish sleep (mucus cocoon); surgeonfish retreat to crevices
  - Moray eels hunt
  - Cardinalfish (Apogonidae) emerge from daytime shelter
  - Biofluorescence visible: many corals and fish fluoresce red/green
    in blue-enriched light

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
NET EFFECT: Reef is productive 24 hours
  Day  = algal photosynthesis + fish foraging
  Night = coral carnivory + invertebrate activity
```

sections.text: ## Decision Cheat Sheet

metadata.title: Reef Ecology: Zones, Food Webs, Herbivory, Cryptic Fauna

sections.text:
| If you need to diagnose... | Start With | Key Caveat |
|---|---|---|
| Maximum coral cover | Fore-reef slope around 5-15 m depth | Fish diversity and coral cover do not peak identically everywhere. |
| CCA-dominated zone | High-energy reef crest | CCA is both habitat cue and structural cement. |
| Algae-control process | Herbivory maintaining open substrate for coral recruitment | Fishing pressure can drive phase shift even without high nutrients. |
| 1983 Caribbean reef crash | Diadema mass mortality and macroalgal bloom | Disease removed a keystone grazer, not coral directly. |
| Parrotfish byproduct | Sand production by bioerosion and grazing | Parrotfish can both maintain substrate and erode carbonate. |
| Algal phase shift | Switch from coral to macroalgae dominance | Hysteresis makes reversal difficult. |
| Trapezia mutualism | Acropora-dwelling crabs defending against crown-of-thorns starfish | Mutualism is species-specific and habitat-specific. |
| Cryptic biodiversity | Roughly 50-70% of reef species hidden in cavities and rubble | Visual surveys undercount reef diversity. |
| Coral feeding timing | Night polyp extension for zooplankton capture | Daytime productivity is largely symbiont-driven. |
| Mesophotic zone | 30-150 m lower-light reefs | Refugium potential is limited by distinct communities and connectivity. |
